title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative:
1. On July 13, 2022, MoLESS promulgated the Reintegration Programme (Operation and Management) Directives for Returnee Migrant Workers, with clear institutional and procedural outlines for reintegrating Nepali returnee migrant workers. The new directive opens up opportunities for long-term returnee migrant workers to receive economic and psychosocial support from the government and development partners.
2. The MoLESS passed two working guidelines on December 11 to expand the social security scheme. The new guidelines cover migrant workers, informal sector workers, and self-employed persons. The government launched the scheme for migrant workers on March 22, 2023. According to Department of Social Security Fund data, 216,000 Nepali migrant workers have joined as of July 15, 2023. Once the new scheme is fully rolled out, it is expected that a large number of Nepalese who are working abroad will have access to social security. 1. With support from the Swiss Development Cooperation, the ILO provided technical assistance to the MoLESS in developing a background paper on reintegration in 2021, which provided information on relevant laws, good practices, and relevant international standards and supported the government in making an informed decision while preparing the Directive. The Directive includes provisions such as economic and psycho-social support, returnee workers registration, skills mapping, and partnership with local government and private business organisations for its implementation. 2. With support from the European Union, ILO provided technical comments and recommendations on the draft schemes in line with international standards.
